parameter_basis.compression: Sjolander 2021 sections 2.1 and 3.1 distinguish closed-normal penalty stiffness from tensile and shear interface stiffness. Use the existing cone-wall contact value, 1e12 Pa/m, as a declared contact-compliance scenario. This is not a measured CL100H interface stiffness or a fitted LVDT value.
parameter_basis.bulk: Sjolander 2021 section 3.1 uses 20 GPa for shotcrete in a different block-loaded study. The 20-versus-30-GPa top-layer change tests an independently acting material mechanism; it is not a modulus inferred from CL100H cubes, raw piston strokes or DOFS. Retain the existing 35-GPa substrate and cone.
parameter_basis.history: Retain the original mixed opening/slip bilinear tensile damage law and its given parameters. Only the undegraded closed-normal stiffness is separated here. Sjolander's pure Mode-I exponential damage law is not being claimed as this implementation.
parameter_basis.materials: Jansson 2024 section 4.5 and the saved raw tests provide cube strength, wedge-splitting force/CMOD and core force, but do not independently identify CL100H bulk moduli or closed-interface stiffness. Jansson 2025 Table 2 reports substrate/FRC failures in the nonglue hydro-demolished cores; it does not identify a unique CL100H interface strength. Its corrigendum text remains unavailable.

question: Do closed-interface compliance and top-layer bulk compliance have distinct effects on the local cone motion and fixed two-depth regional response? Reuse the complete force boundary and reference rather than adjusting observation transfer to fit the same measurements.
